source_review.notes: Checked all ten final NASA references on 2026-08-31; every URL returned HTTP 200. Reviewed Systems Engineering fundamentals, NASA lifecycle phases, Phase E operations/sustainment, Phase F closeout, Product Transition and Integration, cost-effectiveness, Configuration Management, Phase E systems engineering, and NPR 7123.1B. NASA phase names are explicitly treated as one governable lifecycle model rather than universal terminology.

evidence: Reviewed lifecycle value vector L(a)=(E,C,S,R,X) and every dimension definition.
Reviewed present-cost expression with initial, annual, retirement, horizon, and discount terms.
Reviewed stages P, maturity state M_i, stochastic variables Z, and retirement obligation set D.
Confirmed financial cost notation does not absorb mandatory effectiveness, safety, security, legal, environmental, or retirement constraints.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Symbols are defined locally with explicit time, scope, uncertainty, and decision-boundary limitations.

evidence: Executed lifecycle-present-cost-fixture under python3 with exact output in artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-081/report.json.
Confirmed at 5% over eight operating years A present cost is 39.14206887 and B is 34.80264081.
Confirmed rounded values 39.14 and 34.80 and A-minus-B difference 4.34.
Recomputed undiscounted totals A=46 and B=39.
Confirmed cost-only decision is explicitly marked insufficient.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic cash flows omit uncertainty, escalation, quantity, failures, effectiveness, risk, externalities, mission extension, and retirement feasibility.

evidence: Confirmed lifecycle phase progression does not entail one-pass or waterfall technical processes.
Confirmed prototype conformance does not entail stable production capability or operational readiness.
Confirmed physical/product transition does not entail transfer of knowledge, support, authority, data, facilities, or residual risk.
Confirmed lower present cost does not entail preferred alternative under effectiveness, constraints, uncertainty, and tail risk.
Confirmed powered-off status does not entail complete retirement while interfaces, identities, data, hazards, contracts, assets, or records remain.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The chapter uses implication limits and lifecycle counterexamples without claiming a universal optimization theorem.

evidence: Challenged prototype-to-production yield, supplier/process/part-number drift, sole sources, obsolescence, variants, tooling, inspection, and spares.
Challenged handover, competence, facilities, data/rights, credentials, operational limits, workarounds, telemetry bias, maintenance, and knowledge loss.
Challenged upgrades, mixed versions, migration, rollback, threat/policy change, operational anomalies, mission extension, qualified life, and retirement margin.
Challenged cost scope/horizon/rate/escalation/uncertainty, effectiveness, externalities, residual value, sunk-cost reasoning, and tail consequences.
Challenged shutdown, residual clients/jobs/keys/data/hazards/contracts/facilities, privacy/legal records, supplier exit, workforce transition, and long-term liability.
Reviewed all ten examples and five complete answers for assumptions, intermediate reasoning, evidence limits, and bounded conclusions.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Real lifecycle reviews require applicable stakeholder, product, manufacturing, supply, operations, maintenance, human, cost, safety, security, environmental, legal/records, configuration, and closeout expertise.

evidence: Confirmed every decision records outcome, alternatives, assumptions, boundary, evidence, uncertainty, authority, and downstream consequences.
Confirmed end and enabling products mature together from concept through retirement.
Confirmed production variation and operational upgrades remain under design/configuration authority and appropriate V&V.
Confirmed operational learning updates requirements, hazards, models, support, training, and future designs.
Confirmed assumption validity and technical authority persist across organizational transitions.
Confirmed retirement is funded, designed, executed, verified, archived, and assigned residual ownership.
invariant_checking.notes: No phase gate, prototype, part number, delivery, uptime, patch, cost figure, continued function, or power-off event is treated as sufficient alone.

proof_review.notes: No formal proof or theorem requires proof review; the module presents lifecycle structure and bounded present-cost arithmetic.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is labeled or presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: Executable output is labeled synthetic_deterministic_cash_flows_only.
Fixture limitations disclaim effectiveness, uncertainty, production, failures, escalation, externalities, extension, and retirement feasibility.
Examples and exercises are teaching cases, not actual cost estimates, readiness reviews, operational approvals, or disposal decisions.
Official sources are attributed without claiming NASA review or endorsement.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Synthetic calculations, source-backed guidance, internal review, program evidence, and authorized lifecycle decisions remain distinct.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked tailored/non-waterfall lifecycle models, whole-enterprise boundaries, alternative commitment, end/enabling maturity, production, transition, operations, sustainment, evolution, cost/risk, assumptions, extension, retirement, closeout, and residual ownership.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked manufacturability, supply, acceptance, configuration, knowledge/skills transfer, operational baselines, telemetry/workarounds, controlled upgrades, lifecycle cost assumptions, retirement inventories, shutdown/migration/data handling, disposal verification, archive, and lessons.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from concept and alternatives through production, transition, operations, evolution, extension, and retirement. Ten examples and five complete solutions cover sensors, services, suppliers, handover, aging, schemas, predictive maintenance, variants, cloud retirement, and hazardous facilities.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external NASA expert, stakeholder, manufacturer, supplier, operator, maintainer, cost analyst, safety/security authority, environmental specialist, legal/records/privacy authority, configuration manager, closeout organization, or other external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
